Sample Size or Power Calculation for One-Sample Binomial Proportion Test (Two-Sided)

Source: R/one_bino_size.R
one_bino_size.Rd

This function calculates either the required sample size or the achieved power for a two-sided test of a single binomial proportion. It uses a normal approximation to the binomial distribution for testing whether the true proportion differs from a hypothesized value.

Usage

one_bino_size(p, p0, alpha, beta = NULL, n = NULL)

Arguments

p

Numeric. The true proportion under the alternative hypothesis.

p0

Numeric. The hypothesized proportion under the null hypothesis.

alpha

Numeric. Significance level (Type I error rate).

beta

Numeric (optional). Type II error rate (1 - power). Required when calculating the required sample size.

n

Integer (optional). Sample size. Required when calculating power.

Value

  • If beta is provided and n is NULL, returns the required sample size (rounded up).

  • If n is provided and beta is NULL, returns the achieved power of the test.

Details

The function uses the normal approximation to the binomial distribution. It assumes a two-sided z-test for a single binomial proportion.

Examples

# Required sample size for testing p = 0.55 vs p0 = 0.5
one_bino_size(p = 0.55, p0 = 0.5, alpha = 0.05, beta = 0.2)
#> [1] 778

# Power with fixed sample size
one_bino_size(p = 0.55, p0 = 0.5, alpha = 0.05, n = 100)
#> [1] 0.1713209
